speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you mentioned fatigue, flank pain, and fever following recent antibiotic treatment for acute sinusitis; can you tell me if you have experienced any changes in your urine color, frequency, or clarity?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the pain in your flank radiated to your groin, and do you notice any blood or cloudiness in your urine? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Leukocyturia Present, Bacterial Culture Negative, Cytospin Stained With Hansel's Solution: 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those results; the presence of binucleated eosinophilic cells alongside a negative bacterial culture strongly suggests drug-induced interstitial nephritis rather than a typical infection. Did you recently start a new antibiotic, such as amoxicillin-clavulanate, for your sinusitis, or did you have any other new medications or allergies?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Drug-Induced Interstitial Nephritis (AIN) secondary to amoxicillin exposure.

Given your history of a rash after starting amoxicillin for sinusitis, followed by the persistence of fever, flank pain, and leukocyturia with eosinophilic crystals, this is highly consistent with a hypersensitivity reaction affecting the kidneys. Do you currently have any other symptoms like joint pain or a new rash, and when exactly did the flank pain begin relative to the antibiotic change?
